text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.1% today as oil prices pushed higher on Middle East tensions. Brent crude closed above $101 a barrel—the highest level since May—driven by escalating U.S.-Iran conflict and concerns that fighting in the Persian Gulf could disrupt energy supplies. As an oil major, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when crude prices climb, since higher oil prices translate to stronger profits on its production.

The stock has gained 3.6% over the past two weeks as this geopolitical risk premium has built into energy markets. The broader pattern is clear: each new report of military escalation or supply-risk pushes oil higher, and integrated oil companies like this one move in lockstep with those gains.
